CONFIRM C0021 — `_run_tool()` returns `CompletedProcess(..., stderr="TIMEOUT")` on timeout, but `run_pyright/run_ruff/run_bandit/run_mypy` only special-case `"NOT_FOUND"`. For timed-out tools, they proceed to parse empty stdout and silently return `[]`, making timeout indistinguishable from “no issues.” This is a HIGH correctness bug because health scan and fix evaluation can report clean results when analysis never completed.

EXTEND C0021 | FOLLOW: the same timeout swallowing also corrupts `evaluate_fix()`. `_count_tool_issues()` calls the runners both before and after patching; if a tool times out in both phases, pre/post counts become zero and `_compute_fix_verdict()` can classify the fix as `SAFE` or `NEUTRAL` even though no analyzer completed. This crosses the interface into `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` Stage 4, where `SAFE/NEUTRAL` marks findings `verified=True`, enabling the NK “bug closed” gate on unevaluated fixes.

CONFIRM C0001 — `scan_health()` sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` whenever the runner returns without raising. Since missing-tool cases return `[]` instead of raising, unavailable analyzers are reported as available. That directly misleads downstream consumers of `HealthScan.tools_available`.

MERGE C0001 <- F001

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox test execution against the patched source tree. In `bench/endocrine.py`, it copies only the target file into a temp directory as `patched_path`, but when `test_cmd` is provided it runs `_run_tool(test_cmd, cwd=tmpdir)`. The supplied command is not rewritten to point at the sandboxed file/tree, and no package tree is copied. In the actual caller (`immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()`), the command is `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`, which resolves from `cwd=tmpdir` to a non-existent `tmpdir/bench/tests/`; if the command instead uses absolute paths or imports the package from elsewhere, tests exercise the real checkout, not the patched file. Evidence: patched file is written only to `tmpdir/<basename>`, never to `tmpdir/bench/...`, and the command is passed through unchanged.
FOLLOW: This breaks the advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” feature on the happy path. Tests either fail spuriously because the test path no longer exists in the temp dir, causing good fixes to be marked `HARMFUL`, or they run against the real repository/import path and do not validate the patched source at all, causing false `SAFE` classifications. Downstream, `immune_agents` uses these verdicts to set `verified=True`; false negatives suppress valid fixes, while false positives can close bugs based on tests that never touched the patch. The interface crossed is `EndocrineLayer.evaluate_fixes()` → `immune_agents` Stage 4 verification/closure logic.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when evaluating a fix, copy the minimal project subtree needed for execution into the temp dir, preserving the target file’s relative path, write the patch into that copied tree, and run `test_cmd` against paths inside the temp dir. Simplest sufficient version: compute the target file’s repo-relative path, create that path under `tmpdir`, copy `bench/` tests into `tmpdir/bench/`, and execute the same pytest command with `cwd=tmpdir` so imports and test paths resolve to the sandboxed tree.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can mark a fix `SAFE` even when it introduces new issues in one tool, as long as another tool’s count decreases enough to make the summed net negative. Evidence: it computes `total_net = net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues`; only `total_net > 0` is `HARMFUL`, while any `total_net < 0` is `SAFE`. Example: `net_type_errors=+3`, `net_ruff_errors=-5`, `net_bandit_issues=0` yields `SAFE` despite introducing three new type errors.
FOLLOW: This violates the stated contract “SAFE: no new issues introduced.” A fix that worsens type safety or security can still be marked safe because style/lint reductions offset it numerically. Downstream consequence is high: `immune_agents` Stage 4 treats `SAFE` and `NEUTRAL` as sufficient to set `verified=True`, so a fix that introduces real regressions can close the bug and suppress future reports through NK dedup/bug-closed logic. This crosses the endocrine→immune verification interface and produces silently wrong reviewer guidance.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — judge harm per tool, not by summed net. In `_compute_fix_verdict()`, return `HARMFUL` if any of `net_type_errors > 0`, `net_ruff_errors > 0`, or `net_bandit_issues > 0`; return `SAFE` only if at least one net is negative and none are positive; otherwise keep the existing no-change/test handling.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.80
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `run_pyright()` loses diagnostics on the normal “errors found” path when pyright writes JSON to stderr instead of stdout. `_run_tool()` captures both streams, but `run_pyright()` only parses `result.stdout` and ignores `result.stderr` except for the sentinel `"NOT_FOUND"`. Many CLIs emit machine-readable output to stderr on nonzero exit; this wrapper assumes stdout-only and turns such runs into parse failure + empty diagnostics.
FOLLOW: The health scan can report zero pyright findings even though pyright executed and found issues. In fix evaluation, pre/post type-error baselines also become wrong, so `_compute_fix_verdict()` can misclassify patches. This affects both major endocrine outputs: `HealthScan` and `FixEvaluation`, and can flow into immune Stage 4 verified-fix marking.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — in `run_pyright()`, choose the JSON payload from `result.stdout` if non-empty, otherwise from `result.stderr` when it looks like JSON; parse that payload instead of stdout only.
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — fix evaluation compares diagnostics on a single copied file only, but many proposed fixes are module/interface changes whose correctness depends on the surrounding package. Evidence: pre/post counts are gathered by `_count_tool_issues(tool_runner, target_path_or_patched_path)` with one file path, and the sandbox contains only `os.path.basename(target_path)`. Pyright/mypy/bandit/ruff results for an isolated file can differ materially from results in the real package because imports, sibling modules, and package roots are absent.
FOLLOW: A patch can be declared `SAFE` because the isolated file shows fewer errors, while the real codebase would fail once integrated; conversely, an actually safe patch can be marked harmful because isolated analysis cannot resolve imports. This makes the “whole-body” fix-evaluation signal non-representative and contaminates downstream verified-fix closure in `immune_agents`. The broken interface is between endocrine’s sandbox model and the package-oriented analyzers it invokes.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — evaluate pre/post analyzer counts against the copied sandbox project context rather than a lone file. Simplest sufficient fix: copy the source files from `source_paths` into a mirrored temp tree, patch only the target file within that tree, and run each tool over the sandboxed `source_paths` counterpart set instead of a single basename file.
VERIFIED: TRUE
